# What we're building toward

*What the product promises **by launch**, drawn only from what is approved and ticketed for launch. Nothing aspirational, nothing from the draft pile. **Write copy from this section, not from the lists below.***

**Someone starts something.** They tap one control and are asked a single question first: what are you starting? A shop, a gathering, a group. Whatever they pick, the same thing happens underneath — they get a Page — but they are never told to open a shop in order to do something that isn't a shop. The flow speaks their language and offers the tools their thing needs. It takes a few minutes: a name, a real address or just a neighbourhood if they'd rather, a photo, a couple of sentences, and their own words for what it is. If they close it halfway it picks up where they left off.

**What they get is a place of their own.** A Page with a face on it — their photo, or generated art if they don't have one, because nothing is allowed to look abandoned. They can list what they make, what they do, and when people can come. They can change any of it later. If they've got more than one thing going on, they hold more than one Page, and none of them is silently chosen for them.

**How people find them.** Anyone can browse and search without an account and without hitting a wall. The feed is scoped to their metro and ordered by where they are, how recent it is, and what they said they're interested in — never by what keeps them scrolling, and never by anyone paying for placement. Someone searching for sourdough finds the bakers. A Page carries the words its owner chose for it, so it gets found by them. There's a map, and there's a list, and one button to move between them.

**And people can turn up.** Someone can say they're coming. The person who made the thing sees who. That's the point of the whole exercise — the app exists to get people into the same room, not to keep them on a screen.

**Everyone is accountable and nobody is exposed.** Signing up asks for a real legal name, an email, and a zip code, and that's all. The zip suggests a nearby metro; the person still picks. Everyone else sees whatever display name they chose. **Two people who actually deal with each other — a sale, a gathering someone turned up to — see each other's real names, for twelve months, and no other route reaches a name.** No search by name, no lookup, no roster. Anything reported gets hidden immediately and the person who posted it is told why, in plain words, within seconds.

## What is committed for launch but at risk

**Say nothing in copy that depends on these until they land.**

- **Signing in is broken in three separate ways right now** [#67, #69, #74 — all launch-blocking]. The only door into the product does not reliably open.
- **Photographs.** The takedown path shipped, which unblocked them, but no composer attaches a photo yet [#26, #27]. **A launch with no photos on anything is a real possibility.**
- **Saying you're coming** [F063 · #34] is approved and ticketed and not started. Without it a gathering page cannot collect a single response, and half the paragraph above stops being true.
- **The one-create-flow ruling** [F087] is a draft from today. The launch promise in the first paragraph rests on it.
- **Signup as described** [F081, F082] is approved with eight tickets and nothing built.
- **Every word above is written in components, not a copy module** [F084, ~3–4 days, draft]. Changing the launch copy after launch is a developer job until that lands.

# Built — live in production now

*Proof: present in the `origin/main` tree plus the migration or merged PR that put it there.*

- Browse a feed near you without signing in · search, filter, list-or-map — `/`, `/explore`
- **Browse Pages rather than individual listings** — PR #60
- **A metro-scoped feed** — `3b86abd`
- Open any listing; look at anyone's public page — `/m/[handle]`, `/p/[...slug]`
- Sign in by magic link — *three launch-blocking bugs open against it*
- Pick a hood and metro after signup — `/onboarding`
- **Be asked for a metro at every signup, never skipped** — PR #86
- **Join the waitlist for a metro that isn't open, and see where it stands** — PR #86
- Open a shop; list a product, a service, or a gathering — `/you/sell`
- **Tag a Page in your own words instead of picking a category** — PR #66
- **Report something; a reported Page's photo hides at once** — PRs #81, #82
- See what you follow — `/you/following`

**Wired to nothing:** `page_posts` [PR #85] has **no reader and no writer** — its only two mentions outside its own migration are comments saying the table does not exist. Its relationship to items is unstated; see `ITEMS-QUESTION.md`.

**Broken in shipped code:** nobody can say they're coming (responses table has four readers, no writer) · Browse sorts by a column that's always zero · following a business Page tells the app you own a shop · storage access tests have never run.

# Evidence and known drift

*Subordinate to the lists above. **All of this, plus the method failures below, is captured as `socialus-web` #96.***

1. A hand-maintained handoff list said the metro waitlist was awaiting build. It was live [PR #86]. That document is deleted (2026-09-16); the drift is why.
2. Issues #51 and #52 are open against shipped work.
3. `surfaces.md` calls `/join` a redirect shim. It is a 178-line pitch page [#90].
4. `surfaces.md` says the composer renders the twelve retired category terms. The tag step shipped [PR #66].
5. `STATUS.md` is dated 2026-09-08 and predates the report path, the waitlist, tags, and every ruling since.
6. `BUILD-LOG.md` still names the project `movers-makers-shakers/web` and points at a bundle path that doesn't exist.
7. Members have no zip and no legal-name column. But `zip_metro_crosswalk` and `metro_polygons` already exist [migrations 025, 031] — **the zip-to-metro lookup has substrate and T162 is smaller than its ticket implies.**
8. Two report paths live on `main` at once [#63].
9. The only transactional email a member receives is a Supabase dashboard template, outside version control [#74]. `FOLLOW_EMAIL_FROM` still reads *Movers, Makers & Shakers*.
10. **Disputed, not drift: whether `systems/item.md` describes a retired model.** `model.md` carries a section headed "There are no Items"; `item.md` specifies seven kinds and their child tables. **Don disputes that these are the same claim — see `ITEMS-QUESTION.md`. Unresolved.** Both the `items` tables and `page_posts` are live on `main` at once — **two models running side by side, with composers on the retired one and no writer on the new one.** Banner on `item.md` says disputed, not superseded.
11. **`page_posts` has no `recurrence_rule`.** `item_gatherings` does, and `item.md` § Recurring gatherings designs the behaviour. **A recurring gathering cannot be expressed in the new model today** — F074 covers it and is `draft`.

# Regenerating this

**Four checks any regeneration must encode**, each from a mistake made building the first version — all four are in #96:

- `git fetch --all --prune` before reading anything, in every repo.
- **Never `git branch --no-merged` here.** This repo squash-merges, so a merged branch's tip is never an ancestor of `main` and is listed unmerged forever. Use `gh pr list --state merged` or `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.
- An issue's state is not proof of what is on `main`, and `main` is not proof of an issue's state.
- Look for an existing measurement before making one with a grep.

**What a script can do:** everything under *Built*, *To build*, *To retire*, and *Evidence* — they are joins over scenario frontmatter, issues, merged PRs, the `origin/main` tree, and the migrations.

**What it cannot:** *What we're building toward* is judgement, and so is knowing that a gathering composer existing still means hosting starts in a selling flow. **That section is why this document exists, and it needs an agent reading code every time.**
